description: Who moves Kenya's budget forward - Treasury, citizens, Parliament, the Executive, and implementation - in five clear stages for FY2026/27.
footerBody: We'll take you through the full budget-making process - from Treasury formulation to implementation - and show you how you, as a Mwananchi, can take part at every stage.

items.title: National Treasury - Budget Formulation
items.description: Treasury sets the fiscal frame for FY2026/27: MTEF ceilings to ministries and counties, then the Budget Policy Statement projecting KES 3.3T revenue and KES 4.2T expenditure under the BETA agenda.

items.title: Citizens - Public Participation
items.description: Kenyans engage through county hearings, memoranda, and civic forums. Communities and civil society submit input while the Budget and Appropriations Committee is still reviewing estimates.

items.title: Parliament - Review & Approval
items.description: After public hearings, the National Assembly scrutinises the estimates (KES 4.82T), adopts amendments, and approves the budget - including KES 781.4B for education and KES 175.5B for health.

items.title: Executive - Budget Reading & Assent
items.description: Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi presents the KES 4.82T Budget Statement to Parliament. The President assents to the Finance Bill and Appropriation Act, authorising spending for the new financial year.

items.title: Government - Implementation Begins
items.description: FY2026/27 starts on 1 July under the Treasury’s Budget Sasa ni Delivery push - ministries, counties, and agencies turn approved allocations into services citizens can track through BNS.
